title: Tanzanian Beef Wet Fry
community: Enjoyed nationwide — popular restaurant and home dish
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Beef Wet Fry — tender beef strips stir-fried with onions, tomatoes, green pepper, and spices in a bold, slightly reduced sauce. Tanzania's most popular restaurant beef dish — somewhere between a stir-fry and a quick braise, deeply flavourful and fast to make.
longDesc: Beef wet fry is the restaurant beef dish of urban Tanzania — quick to make, intensely flavoured, and served at every restaurant and food court in Dar es Salaam. The "wet" refers to the saucy, slightly glossy consistency that distinguishes it from a dry fry.
steps: Heat pan over very high heat until smoking.
Add oil. Sear beef strips in batches — 2 minutes. Remove.
Add onions, garlic, ginger. Stir-fry 3 minutes.
Add bell pepper and tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes.
Add cumin, paprika, soy sauce, salt, and pepper.
Add a splash of water. Cook 3—4 minutes until sauce is glossy and slightly reduced.
chefTips: Very high heat throughout — this is a stir-fry, not a simmer.
Sear beef in small batches — crowding steams instead of sears.
The soy sauce is the umami secret — do not skip.
cookingScience: The "wet" in wet fry comes from the addition of a small amount of water in the final stage — it creates steam that carries the spice flavours into the meat while simultaneously concentrating the sauce through evaporation.
culturalNote: Beef wet fry is the lunch dish of Tanzania's urban office workers — the restaurant dish that is available everywhere, ready in 10 minutes, and consistently satisfying.
